facts.statement: Aurorazhdarcho lived during the early Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic in what is now Bavaria, southern Germany.
facts.quote: Aurorazhdarcho is an extinct genus of ctenochasmatoid pterosaur known from the Late Jurassic period (early Tithonian stage) of what is now Bavaria, southern Germany.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Aurorazhdarcho micronyx is considered one of the earliest, if not the very first, documented pterosaur fossils ever found.
facts.quote: A specimen, originally classified as Pterodactylus micronyx (now Aurorazhdarcho micronyx), was one of the earliest, if not the earliest, documented pterosaur fossil ever found.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, known as the Pester Exemplar, was likely unearthed between 1757 and 1779.
facts.quote: Evidence suggest that the Pester Exemplar was unearthed at some point between 1757, when Maria Anna was recovering from serious cases of pneumonia and tuberculosis, after which she began collecting fossils, and 1779, when the specimen was first studied by scientists.

facts.statement: When first studied by Ignaz von Born, the holotype specimen was misidentified as a decapod crustacean due to its unusual anatomy.
facts.quote: Because of this, and the unusual (and at the time totally unknown) anatomy of pterosaurs, the specimen was originally misidentified as a decapod crustacean when it was first studied by Ignaz von Born, a prominent Enlightenment naturalist.

facts.statement: The Pester Exemplar was re-discovered in 1982, restoring its status as the type specimen for Pterodactylus micronyx.
facts.quote: The Pester Exemplar was re-discovered in 1982, during a re-organization of the collections in Eötvös Loránd University, and so the status of type specimen for P. micronyx reverted to it.

facts.statement: An adult Aurorazhdarcho fossil was uncovered in 1999 by amateur paleontologist Peter Kaszmekat in the Blumenberg Quarry near Eichstätt.
facts.quote: In 1999, amateur paleontologist Peter Kaszmekat uncovered a fossil of a pterosaur in the Blumenberg Quarry, 3 km northwest of Eichstätt, in layers of the Solnhofen limestone.

facts.statement: The species Aurorazhdarcho primordius was named and described in 2011 by Eberhard Frey, Christian A. Meyer, and Helmut Tischlinger.
facts.quote: Based on the specimen, the type species Aurorazhdarcho primordius was named and described by Eberhard Frey, Christian A. Meyer and Helmut Tischlinger in 2011.

facts.statement: The genus name Aurorazhdarcho combines the Latin word for dawn and the Kazakh name for a mythical dragon.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin aurora, "dawn" and Kazakh Azhdarcho, the name of a mythical dragon.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a nearly complete skeleton preserved on a single slab, though it lacks the skull and neck.
facts.quote: It consists of a nearly complete skeleton, three-dimensionally preserved on a single slab with the counterplate having been removed, lacking the skull and neck.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the animal died after a predator attack that nearly ripped off its head and neck, causing the body to sink quickly.
facts.quote: That the head and neck are now absent is explained by the animal being killed by a partially failed attack by a predator, almost ripping off these parts, after which the body quickly sank.

facts.statement: The holotype individual was likely a subadult male, indicated by fused ischiopubes and the absence of a wide birth canal.
facts.quote: The individual was probably subadult and, as indicated by the fusion of the ischiopubes in the pelvis, a male as it lacks a wide birth canal.

facts.statement: Bennett concluded that Aurorazhdarcho primordius and Pterodactylus micronyx are the same species, treating primordius as a junior synonym of micronyx.
facts.quote: Bennett concluded that Aurorazhdarcho primordius and "Pterodactylus" micronyx are in fact conspecific; he retained Aurorazhdarcho as a genus distinct from Pterodactylus, but he considered the specific epithet primordius to be a junior synonym of the epithet micronyx.

facts.statement: A 2025 study concluded that both Aurorazhdarcho primordius and Pterodactylus micronyx are junior synonyms of Gnathosaurus subulatus.
facts.quote: In a 2025 study Bennett compared fossil material of Gnathosaurus subulatus with skulls of the largest juvenile specimens of "Pterodactylus" micronyx, and concluded that both "Pterodactylus" micronyx and Aurorazhdarcho primordius are indeed junior synonyms of Gnathosaurus subulatus.

facts.statement: Aurorazhdarcho was a relatively small pterosaur with a wingspan of 537.8 mm based on the type specimen.
facts.quote: Aurorazhdarcho was a relatively small pterosaur. The combined elements of a single wing of the type specimen have the extended length of 537.8 mm.

facts.statement: Fossil impressions indicate that Aurorazhdarcho had an elongated head with a high-positioned eye socket.
facts.quote: The impressions indicate the head was elongated with the eye socket in a high position.

facts.statement: The snout of Aurorazhdarcho may have carried a high, rounded crest.
facts.quote: The snout might have carried a high, rounded, crest.

facts.statement: Neck impressions show that Aurorazhdarcho had a relatively short neck with signs of a throat pouch.
facts.quote: The impression of the neck is relatively short and shows signs of a throat pouch.

facts.statement: Aurorazhdarcho had relatively long legs, with the shinbone being over a third longer than the thighbone.
facts.quote: The legs were relatively long with the shinbone over a third longer than the thighbone.

facts.statement: The wing metacarpals of Aurorazhdarcho were very elongated, with the fourth metacarpal longer than the lower arm.
facts.quote: In the wing the metacarpals were very elongated, the fourth metacarpal being longer than the lower arm.

facts.statement: Bennett suggested Aurorazhdarcho's interlocking teeth formed a basket for sieving food, functioning like spoonbill jaws for wading and catching individual prey.
facts.quote: The upper and lower teeth interlocked; according to Bennett (2013) they formed a basket for sieving food items from water, though the lack of a pumping mechanism suggests a function more akin to spoonbill jaws, wading with the jaws open and closing them when catching individual prey, much as in other ctenochasmatoids.

facts.statement: An amateur paleontologist named Peter Katschmekat discovered a pterosaur fossil in the Blumenberg Quarry in 1999.
facts.quote: En 1999 el paleontólogo aficionado Peter Katschmekat descubrió un fósil de un pterosaurio en la Cantera Blumenberg

facts.statement: The genus Aurorazhdarcho was named by Eberhard Frey, Christian A. Meyer, and Helmut Tischlinger in 2011 based on this specimen.
facts.quote: Basándose en este espécimen, el género Aurorazhdarcho fue nombrado por Eberhard Frey, Christian A. Meyer y Helmut Tischlinger en 2011

facts.statement: Aurorazhdarcho lived during the early Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 150 million years ago, in the Solnhofen Limestone area of Eichstätt.
facts.quote: Fue extraído de la Caliza de Solnhofen en el área de Eichstätt, datando de principios de la etapa del Titoniense del Jurásico Superior, hace cerca de 150 millones de años

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single nearly complete skeleton preserved in three dimensions.
facts.quote: Aurorazhdarcho es conocido a partir de un único esqueleto casi completo preservado en tres dimensiones

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, NMB Sh 110, was found in the upper part of the Eichstätt Formation dating to the early Tithonian of the Late Jurassic, about 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Aurorazhdarcho, NMB Sh 110, fue hallado en la parte superior de la formación Eichstätt datando de principios de la etapa del Titoniense del Jurásico Superior, hace unos 150 millones de años

facts.statement: The absence of the head and neck is explained by the animal dying from a partially failed predator attack that nearly tore these parts off.
facts.quote: El que la cabeza y el cuello estén ausentes se explica por el hecho de que animal murió en un ataque parcialmente fallido de un depredador, casi arrancando estas partes

facts.statement: The individual was likely a subadult male, indicated by the fused ischiopubis in the pelvis and the lack of a wide egg-laying canal.
facts.quote: El individuo era probablemente un subadulto y era, como indica la fusión de los isquiopubis en la pelvis, un macho ya que carecía de un amplio canal de puesta

facts.statement: Aurorazhdarcho was a relatively small pterosaur with a combined wing element span of 537.8 millimeters.
facts.quote: Aurorazhdarcho era un pterosaurio relativamente pequeño. Los elementos combinados de una única ala del espécimen tipo tiene una longitud extendida de 537,8 milímetros

facts.statement: Impressions indicate the head was elongated with the eye socket in a high position.
facts.quote: Las impresiones indican que la cabeza era alargada con la cuenca ocular en una posición alta

facts.statement: The snout may have had a high rounded crest.
facts.quote: El hocico puede haber tenido una cresta alta redondeada

facts.statement: The neck impression is relatively short and shows signs of having a gular sac.
facts.quote: La impresión del cuello es relativamente corta y muestra signos de tener un saco gular

facts.statement: The shoulder girdle was reconstructed with a low shoulder joint.
facts.quote: La cintura escapular fue reconstruida por los autores con una articulación baja en el hombro

facts.statement: The legs were relatively long, with the tibia nearly one-third longer than the femur.
facts.quote: Las patas eran relativamente largas con la tibia cerca de un tercio más larga que el fémur

facts.statement: In the wing, the metacarpals were very elongated, with the fourth metacarpal longer than the forearm.
facts.quote: En el ala los metacarpianos eran muy alargados, siendo el cuarto metacarpiano más largo que el antebrazo

facts.statement: The genus authority is Frey, Meyer & Tischlinger, 2011.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Frey, Meyer & Tischlinger, 2011

facts.statement: The type species is Aurorazhdarcho micronyx.
facts.quote: type_species: Aurorazhdarcho micronyx

facts.statement: Synonyms include Pterodactylus micronyx von Meyer, 1856 and Aurorazhdarcho primordius Frey et al., 2011.
facts.quote: synonyms: Pterodactylus nettecephaloides Ritgen, 1826 (nomen oblitum) Ornithocephalus redenbacheri Wagner, 1851 (nomen oblitum) Pterodactylus longirostris von Meyer, 1859 Pterodactylus brevirostris von Meyer, 1859 Pterodactylus micronyx von Meyer, 1856 Pterodactylus pulchellus von Meyer, 1861 Aurorazhdarcho primordius Frey et al., 2011

facts.quote: familia: Ctenochasmatidae

facts.quote: subordo: Pterodactyloidea

facts.statement: Originally, describers assigned Aurorazhdarcho to the superfamily Azhdarchoidea and placed it in a new family, Protazhdarchidae, of which it is the only named member.

facts.statement: Bennett in 2013 concluded that the genus is actually a ctenochasmatid based on analysis of specimens attributed to Aurorazhdarcho micronyx, considering its short neck and foot morphology.
facts.quote: Bennett en 2013, basándose en el análisis de los especímenes atribuidos a Aurorazhdarcho micronyx (antes incluido en Pterodactylus) y tomando en cuenta su cuello corto y la morfología del pie, llegó a la conclusión de que el género es en realidad un ctenocasmátido

facts.statement: The time range for Aurorazhdarcho is from 149.2 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a nearly complete skeleton preserved in three dimensions on a single rock slab, from which the counter-mold was removed, lacking the skull and neck.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Aurorazhdarcho, NMB Sh 110, fue hallado en la parte superior de la formación Eichstätt datando de principios de la etapa del Titoniense del Jurásico Superior, hace unos 150 millones de años. Consiste en un esqueleto casi completo, preservado tridimensionalmente en una única lámina de roca, cuyo contramolde fue removido, y carece del cráneo y el cuello

facts.statement: The missing skull and neck elements are present as impressions because their movement on the lake floor left a natural mold covered by organic remains in the form of calcium phosphate flakes, visible through UV photography by Tischlinger.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estos elementos están presentes como impresiones, ya que el movimiento de estos elementos en el fondo del lago en el que el cadáver descendió dejando un molde natural cubierto por restos orgánicos en la forma de hojuelas de fosfato de calcio que se hicieron visibles a través de la fotografía UV de Tischlinger

facts.statement: Subsequent swelling of the carcass due to decomposition may have caused the head to drift away.
facts.quote: La posterior hinchazón del cadáver por la descomposición pudo haber causado que la cabeza quedara a la deriva

facts.statement: The first to fourth wing finger phalanges have lengths of 119, 70.8, 50.8, and 50.6 millimeters, respectively.
facts.quote: Las falanges primera a la cuarta del dedo del ala tienen longitudes de 119, 70,8, 50,8 y 50,6 milímetros, respectivamente

facts.statement: Describers rejected cladistic analysis, using comparative methods to find similarity to Ctenochasma elegans but concluding it belonged to Azhdarchoidea due to shared key adaptations, most decisively the low shoulder joint.
facts.quote: Los descriptores rechazaron el uso de un análisis cladístico para establecer su filogenia. Usando el método comparativo encontraron que Aurorazhdarcho era similar en sus proporciones al ctenocasmátido Ctenochasma elegans, una especie también hallada en Solnhofen, pero concluyeron que Aurorazhdarcho pertenecía a Azhdarchoidea debido a que compartía ciertas adaptaciones clave con ese grupo, siendo la más decisiva de la que consideraron la articulación baja del hombro

facts.statement: The position of the shoulder joint in Ctenochasma could not be established, but describers assumed it was high due to the close relationship of that taxon with Pterodactylus.
facts.quote: La posición de esa articulación en Ctenochasma no pudo ser establecida pero los descriptores asumieron que era alta debido a la relación cercana de ese taxón con Pterodactylus

facts.statement: It is the oldest known azhdarchoid.
facts.quote: Es el azdarcoideo más antiguo conocido
